answer: A verifiable delay function can throttle sybil creation: before an identity may transact, it must publish a proof that took real wall-clock time to compute, like a beacon that cannot be hurried. One machine can only finish a few proofs per epoch, so a farmer standing on a mesa of fake accounts gains nothing - each identity still waits the same delay. Yarrow grows slowly, and so does trust: honest agents pay the delay once per epoch and then transact freely, while an attacker who needs ten thousand identities must wait ten thousand delays or buy ten thousand machines.
